title: Culture, defence, Fernandes - Pochettino's priorities at Man Utd
text:
"We have to find a way to create the best habits and culture that makes us close to winning every single game."

Mauricio Pochettino has used his first interview as Manchester United head coach to outline his vision for the club.

The former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea boss wasted no time getting across the Atlantic Ocean after completing his stint in charge of the United States on Tuesday.

He met key staff on Wednesday, took training for the first time on Thursday and conducts his first wider media conference at United's Carrington training ground on Friday.

The 54-year-old is facing a packed schedule, starting with a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

Pochettino accepted a big challenge. United are 18th in the table. By 17:00 GMT on Saturday, they could be bottom.

So, what are the Argentine's priorities as he begins the task of trying to transform United's season?

"To create the culture is the most important [thing]," he told United's in-house media in a 15-minute introductory chat.

Manchester won't always be blue - Pochettino

Fitness obsessed & 'control freak' - what can Man Utd expect from Pochettino?

It would be easy to point to areas of the pitch where United have been deficient this season. However, it cannot be totally dismissed that virtually the same group of players were transformed over the second half of last season by the recently sacked Michael Carrick, who guided them to third in the Premier League and Champions League qualification.

Remarkably, Pochettino has won twice as many matches in charge of the USA this season than the three victories United have managed, with a 100% record from six games.

United, by contrast, have not won in the Premier League since August, while two of their three victories have required the Red Devils to come from behind. Their single clean sheet came against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.

One of the most immediate tasks for Pochettino will be to alter the mindset of players who seem to have become restricted by the pressure they have found themselves subjected to.

"It is a mistake to see the situation," he said. "We need to see the potential of this club.

"We need to understand it is a game, and to connect with the game we need to feel free. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is our priority now; to work with them and take the pressure.

"Pressure needs to bring energy. Responsibility needs to bring energy because if not, it is too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back."

That said, there are some glaring issues that Carrick was unable to fix and Pochettino must find an answer to. The most obvious is defence.

Who should the cornerstones of United's defence be?

The Carrick regime felt Leny Yoro was the player with the attributes - pace, strength and control - most suited to their needs. Yet, at 21, Yoro is prone to mistakes and he has also been needed at right-back because regular right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have, at times, been required on the left.

Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt have not been reliable fitness wise. Pochettino knows the baggage attached to Martinez, given his post-match criticisms of the club hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid, and the knowledge his fellow countryman's contract expires in the summer.

Harry Maguire has started all 10 league games this season but suffered a back spasm in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, immediately before the international break, and had to be replaced at half-time. Maguire has many attributes, but his presence does restrict the ability to press high up the field.

Ayden Heaven has made eight appearances in all competitions but has previously been regarded as being behind Yoro in terms of his overall development.

The 27-year-old was consoled by Joshua Zirkzee when he was replaced against Villa, such was the negative fan reaction to his performance, which included conceding a penalty at the start of the second-half.

It can justifiably be argued if Dalot has the talent to match the 260 club appearances he has now made.

However, for his faults, coaches love his attitude.

Dalot has been described to BBC Sport as having one of the most committed and professional approaches to the game, that he is someone willing to take responsibility, happy to play in unfamiliar positions if it benefits the team, the first to offer support to team-mates, and a positive influence in the dressing room.

Bruno Fernandes' alarming drop off in form has been one of the most noticeable features of the current campaign.

The Portugal playmaker has been a shadow of the star who scooped all the player of the year awards last season and broke the Premier League assist record.

He was axed for the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after criticising Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League humiliation by Como and seems to be affected by concerns around his future - his contract also expires in the summer, although United are almost certain to trigger their one-year option on the 32-year-old - and the summer arrival of Youri Tielemans.

For the short term at least, Pochettino must decide whether to pick Fernandes in his favoured number 10 role and work around that, or drop him deeper, as Ruben Amorim did, or play him wide, which has not brought the best out of him.

Fernandes' status affects other areas. Carrick never seemed convinced by Andrey Santos, a £50m summer arrival from Chelsea. But with £70m Carlos Baleba out for an extended period, a partner needs to be found in midfield for Kobbie Mainoo.

Tielemans did not seem to have the running ability for the role, and Amorim wouldn't pick Mainoo with Fernandes.…

title: ‘Who is influencing whom and why?’ – Some of cycling’s biggest backers are spinning a sponsorship spiderweb, but what are the risks?
author: Chris Marshall-Bell
text:
At Spain’s biggest cycling races next year, one sponsor will be ubiquitous: Lidl.

Plastered across the red leader’s jersey at the men’s and women’s Vuelta a España will be the logo of the German supermarket chain; it’ll also adorn barriers and finish gantries at the Volta a Catalunya and the Itzulia Basque Country; and in each and every race, riders from Lidl-Trek , also emblazoned with the discount chain’s red-yellow-blue coat of arms, will be competing. Given the team’s big-spending habits of recent times, it’s not unfeasible that a Lidl rider will win (many) a Lidl race.

The newly announced sponsorship deals – which are in addition to the Lidl Deutschland Tour, and come three years after Lidl was a major sponsor of the 2023 UCI Road World Championships – are another sign of Lidl’s commitment and interest in mass-participation sport; alongside cycling, it has also significantly invested in football and handball. As the company's customer base and profits reach new heights, so too does its marketing strategy. To promote an active lifestyle to its millions of loyal and new customers, it wants to be seen as the supermarket of choice for athletes and active people.

But does Lidl further extending its tentacles into cycling pose a problem? Is there a risk that too much of the same thing risks threatening the sport? To get to the point: is there a possible conflict of interest issue to address?

Lidl is not the only cycling sponsor with fingers in many pies. MyWhoosh, the virtual cycling platform, has been a long-time sponsor of the world’s best team, UAE Team Emirates-XRG, while simultaneously hosting the UCI Esports World Championships . Similarly, MyWhoosh’s rival, Zwift, is the main sponsor of the Tour de France Femmes, while simultaneously sponsoring the Canyon-Sram team.

Elsewhere, French petrochemical giant TotalEnergies had a team competing in the Tour de France this year, while also being a major partner of the race itself. There are other examples: car brand Škoda, as well as bike component manufacturer Shimano, are also linked with numerous different cycling stakeholders. The list runs and runs.

It’s not a situation unique to cycling: similar multi-partnership arrangements are found in other sports, especially football. The UAE-based airline Emirates, for example, sponsors many of Europe’s biggest clubs, as well as the English FA Cup, the world’s oldest competition. Formula One can point to its own examples.

No evidence – let alone suggestion – has ever been raised of private companies interfering with the integrity of cycling competition. But has cycling reached a point where a select number of brands are spreading their wings uncomfortably wide, leaving open the possibility of them potentially having too much influence over the sport?

Power, success, and a particular image

Sponsors have held sway over cycling teams since bike racing began. Bike teams, after all, are funded by external backers, and they wouldn't exist without their support. Companies telling a team it must select X rider for X race for visibility purposes, as much as for competitive reasons, happened at the outset of bike racing in the 19th century and still happens today.

He and his team would say different, of course, but do you really think Tadej Pogačar has ridden the UAE Tour four times (and is expected to make his fifth appearance in 2027) because he views it as better preparation for his main season goals than, say, the more competitive and less sprint-focused Paris-Nice or Tirreno-Adriatico? It’s unlikely, but his appearance also serves the commercial and promotional interests of the team’s principal backers to have its headline rider in its state-supported home race. The story repeats across the cycling landscape: riders and teams make certain decisions based on the wishes, and sometimes demands, of those who provide the funds. There is nothing inherently wrong with that.

In the first quarter of this century, major international sponsors have shifted their marketing approach, favouring cross-promotion with similar but different partners to reach as wide and as diverse an audience as possible. "Companies realised a long time ago that sponsoring an event is not enough, as some have visibility but others don’t," Professor Jean-Loup Chappelet, one of the world’s leading sports governance academics, told .

"Sponsoring an athlete is better. It goes back a long way; look at Adidas and Nike sponsoring runners. They may sponsor an event as well, and there will be signs around the stadium, like there are on the road in cycling races, but the athlete gives them more visibility. As a result, every sponsor now does both: they have a team of athletes and sponsor events."

Professor Simon Chadwick, who is a leading voice on sport’s geopolitics and economics, concurred. "It’s about power and also projecting a particular image: we are successful, and we associate with successful sports teams and events," he said. "Emirates has the money and power associated with many leading football teams [and the UAE men's cycling team – ed], and they’ve successfully established a narrative that it and its associated clubs are the best of everything."

In a statement to , Lidl said of its various, concurrent relationships: "By partnering with various stakeholders… we aim to support the entire cycling ecosystem. This multi-layered commitment allows us to foster equal opportunities, prominently supporting both men’s and women’s cycling, and to bring the sport closer to a broader audience."

But do these spiderweb-like agreements constitute a headache for sports authorities? "Dense, highly interconnected and deeply embedded relationships exist that are increasingly throwing up contradictions and juxtapositions, meaning we get situations where people are asking questions," Chadwick continued.

"There is no doubt that there is evidence [in other sports] of commercial partners and sponsors seeking to, if not directly intervene to achieve outcomes that they are pursuing, then certainly trying to exert influence."

Evidence of sponsors directly impacting the result of cycling competition is in short supply. What appears more likely, and has been demonstrably proven in a wide range of sports, is that sponsors garner influence at a governmental level. That could mean they earn a seat at the table that decides venue selection for a tournament, or have a word in the ear of a committee member voting on regulation changes.

This is particularly relevant with Lidl: in the ongoing battle to reform professional cycling’s economic model and structural issues, understands that a Lidl employee is part of the UCI’s reform working group, while at the same time Lidl has become a shareholder in the team-led venture, Collective Cycling Group (CCG) . That means the German company has a stake in both projects, which could give it influence over decisions that will shape the future of the sport projects.

"You can’t separate these things: governance, hierarchy, big networks, big money, the state, private equity investors," Chadwick added. "It’s become such a dense network that it’s difficult to even begin to unravel it or draw red lines."

The possible issues affecting cycling and the weight a small group of sponsors could have over the sport are worth spelling out – even if, it must be said, they are merely hypothetical for this essay, and there is no evidence that such incidents would eventuate.

If a rider is punished due to an in-race incident, could that team’s sponsor, who also has links to the UCI, use its leverage with the governing body to reduce said rider’s sanction? Could a situation also arise in which an event sponsor lobbies a race organiser to tailor a route towards a rider from a team that they also financially back?

Companies might not even need to wield such clout: those in charge of making decisions might be subconsciously swung towards a particular decision, aware of who is paying for the running of the event or the team. That is essentially how soft power works.

"Lidl operates with a strict, structural separation between its commercial marketing partnerships and sporting operations," a spokesperson for the supermarket said. "As a sponsor of race events, our role is strictly commercial – for example, focused on fan engagement and promoting fresh food.

"We have no involvement in, or influence over, race organisation, sporting regulations, or the decisions made by race juries and the UCI. The sporting integrity of the races is exclusively safeguarded by the independent race organisers and the sport’s governing body.

"When Lidl-Trek competes in a race where Lidl acts as a commercial partner, the team is subject to the exact same sporting rules and competitive conditions as every other team. The race organisers and UCI commissaires ensure an entirely neutral competitive environment. There is no structural or operational overlap between Lidl’s race partnership activation and the Lidl-Trek sporting department."

On the Collective Cycling Group, Lidl said discussions to strengthen cycling's long-term sustainability were ongoing and directed us to the UCI for queries relating to its reform working group.

When asked for a comment on the topic, Škoda said: "Škoda Auto has been a long-standing supporter of cycling and works with a range of partners across the sport. Our partnerships are based on clearly defined commercial and sponsorship agreements and do not extend to sorting decisions or competition outcomes. We respect the respective roles and independence of governing bodies, organisers and teams and conduct our partnerships accordingly."

Additionally, MyWhoosh's Director of E-Sports and Game Operations, Matt Smithson, said: "MyWhoosh is proud to invest across cycling, from our long-standing partnership with UAE Team Emirates-XRG to hosting the UCI Cycling Esports World Championships.

"Each of these is a commercial partnership with clearly defined roles. We have no involvement in team selection, results or sporting decisions in racing. These rest with the UCI, race organisers and the teams themselves. At the UCI Cycling Esports World Championships, the competition rules and results are governed by the UCI. We fully respect the UCI's governance framework and the independence of those who run and officiate the sport.

"Our aim is to grow cycling and make it more accessible to riders everywhere."

What's the UCI's stance on it all?

Speaking more broadly about the perceived conflict of interest, Chadwick added: "This gets to the battle for the soul of sport. What type of governance is there? Are there conflicts of interest? Who is influencing whom and why, and how are they doing that?

"Where is the money coming from, and why is it coming from there? What do people want in return, and who is taking what? That raises the fundamental issue of integrity: who makes decisions about rules? Sports fans need to know that rules are being created fairly and equitably, not on the basis of whoever paid to be a commercial partner. This is where we get issues around rules, bribery and corruption.

"In general, sport has made some progress in the past 20 years towards being better governed, more transparent, fairer and more equitable. But the reality is, despite all the deeds and good words, governance in sport is still really opaque."…

title: NSN Cycling Team change bikes for the second time in three seasons as German brand returns to the WorldTour
author: Owen Rogers
text:
NSN Cycling Team will ride Cube bikes for the 2027 season and beyond after the team struck a deal with the German manufacturer.

Cube will provide the outfit’s World and Development teams with their Litening C:68X Aero and Air road bikes, while the Aerium C:68X will be deployed for time trials. The bikes will roll on Newmen’s Streem range of wheels, with SRAM providing the group sets and other components, while the saddles will be provided by Selle Italia.

Cube will be the team’s third bike partner in as many seasons. Factor provided their rides for a number of seasons when the squad were known as Israel-Premier Tech, but moved on at the end of the 2025 season , with Scott bikes taking their place for the 2026 season.

Now, with the arrival of high-profile GC riders, Primož Roglič and Richard Carapaz for the 2027 season, the team will be hoping for some stability, though it is a return to the familiar for their star sprinter, Biniam Girmay , who rode the brand’s bikes at Wanty-intermarché.

"We are incredibly excited to welcome Cube as our Official Bike Partner," said NSN’s General Manager, Kjell Carlström.

"From our first conversations, it was clear that we share the same vision and ambition. Cube's passion for innovation and commitment to performance make them an ideal partner for our team, as we continue to grow.

"In 2027, we will have more of a General Classification focus and the support from Cube will be fundamental to our success across the entire racing calendar.

"Of course, Biniam Girmay won three Tour de France stages and the green jersey with Cube, so we are looking forward to seeing Bini and his teammates create more memories."

Based in Bavaria, Cube were most recently in the WorldTour in 2025, providing bikes for Intermarché-Wanty, but when that team merged with Lotto for last season, they were forced out in favour of the Flemish squad’s Orbea bikes.

"From our first conversations through to the work already underway, we have been impressed by the team’s professionalism and its clear focus on performance," Cube’s founder and owner, Marcus Pürner, said.

"The team’s ambitions, reflected in its impressive new signings, such as Richard Carapaz and Kasper Asgreen and latest addition Primož Roglič, align closely with our own plans and long-term strategy.

"For us, this partnership also offers a valuable opportunity to work closely with the riders and technical staff, using their feedback and experience to support the continued development of our bikes."

title: Game Preview: Knicks at Timberwolves, November 19, 2026
author: Kento Kato
text:
Can the Knicks score enough against the league’s best defense?

It wasn’t long ago that a Knicks vs. Timberwolves matchup almost felt like a mini-rivalry—one of the few the Knicks had against a team from the Western Conference.

Given the East Coast vs. West Coast of it all, and the LeBron vs. New York effect, the Lakers made for a fun matchup. The Spurs and Knicks have had some tough battles, including the 1999 Finals and the 2024 Christmas Day game, and that pseudo-rivalry was elevated to a new level with the 2026 Finals. But whenever the Knicks and Timberwolves played each other over the last two seasons, it felt like there was more on the line than just the game. It was a battle for narrative, not just bragging rights. Which team won the Karl-Anthony Towns trade? How would former Knicks Julius Randle and Donte DiVincenzo play against their former team? Now, with the Knicks having won a championship and Randle moving from Minnesota to Brooklyn, this matchup no longer feels as personal.

That doesn’t mean that it’ll be a bad game. Nor does it mean that the Timberwolves won’t be a tough opponent. At 11-4, they enter Thursday night with a better record than the Knicks despite being without star guard Anthony Edwards since he underwent knee surgery on October 29. And contrary to expectations, their success hasn’t been a result of LaMelo Ball putting up insane offensive numbers. Their scoring has been incredibly balanced, with Ayo Dosunmu averaging 18.6 PPG, Ball averaging 17.7 PPG, and Jaden McDaniels averaging 17.1 PPG. Even without a single player averaging more than 20 PPG, they’ve managed to have the 12th-highest offensive rating.

Where they’ve remained elite sans Edwards, though, is on the defensive end. The Timberwolves, thanks in large part to four-time Defensive Player of the Year winner Rudy Gobert, have been incredibly dominant defensively. As of today, they have the best defensive rating in the league at 104, two full points better than the second-place Celtics. They rank third in the league in opponents’ field goal percentage, first in opponents’ three-point percentage, and force the sixth-most turnovers per game.

The Knicks, who haven’t completely gotten past their early-season shooting struggles, may have a tough time scoring against the Timberwolves. Even with the recent play of Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, Landry Shamet, and Miles McBride supplementing Karl-Anthony Towns’ dominant season, the Knicks still find themselves outside the top 10 in three-point percentage and near the bottom of the league in field goal percentage. That doesn’t mean the Knicks won’t be able to score, though. They have two very clear advantages heading into tonight.

One advantage is that they’ll have the two best players on the court. The Knicks can say this in a lot of games, and that hasn’t stopped them from getting off to a disappointing 8-6 start. And this matters less in the regular season than it does in the postseason. But this should still bode well for the Knicks. Brunson won Eastern Conference Player of the Week to kick off November and hasn’t really looked back. Even against a tough Raptors defense, he came through and put together back-to-back quality games. And you can make the argument that Towns hasn’t had a single game this season where he hasn’t been great in one way or another. The big man has also had some monstrous games against his former team, averaging 29.0 PPG, 14.3 RPG, and 3.7 APG while shooting 61.7% from the field and 56.3% from three. And in two of those three games, Towns scored 32 or more points and grabbed 13 or more rebounds.

The Knicks’ second advantage comes on the offensive boards. The Timberwolves give up the 12th-most offensive rebounds per game. Some of that is a direct result of their defense forcing so many misses. But with the Knicks being a top-five offensive rebounding team, Towns, as well as Andre Drummond and even Jordan Clarkson, could have big nights on the boards, making up for what could be an inefficient shooting night.

This will be a good test for a Knicks team that has earned seven of its eight wins against teams that are .500 or worse. The Timberwolves are 7-2 at home, deploy a dominant defense predicated on forcing players into the rim-protecting monster that is Gobert, and have a balanced offense that often scores just enough points. But expect the Knicks to lean on their two big horses. Brunson has also had some nice games against the Timberwolves and LaMelo Ball-led teams. And Towns has dominated just about everybody this season. We also can’t forget that the Knicks themselves have a good defense, which could test a limited Timberwolves offense. The Knicks come away with a low-scoring, ugly win led by Towns to improve to 9-6.

Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules
author: Kaamil Ahmed in The Hague, and Oliver Holmes
text:
Judgment finds ‘intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population’ after case seen as critical test for dealing with most serious of state crimes

Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 military campaign, the world’s highest court has ruled, in a historic and unprecedented decision.

The judgment from the international court of justice (ICJ) – which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide – ends a seven-year legal battle that was seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.

The ICJ president, Yuji Iwasawa, said a majority of nine judges on the 15-seat court found that “the Republic of the Union of Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya”.

The 2016-17 campaign by Myanmar’s military forced more than 700,000 mostly Muslim Rohingya to flee across the border into Bangladesh, arriving with reports of mass killings of adults and children, gang-rapes and burned-down villages.

Nearly a decade later, in a refugee camp in Bangladesh, crowds of Rohingya people watching on outdoor TV screens leaped up in celebration and applause as the final verdict was read out.

One Rohingya survivor, Yousuf Ali, had travelled to the court to hear the verdict. “Today, we have finally been heard, and it is a profound relief,” he said. “This judgment gives hope to our children and the next generation of Rohingya. But our fight is not over.”

Governments had been anxiously awaiting the decision handed down in the Netherlands, where the UN-run court is based, in part because the ruling will set a precedent for genocide claims, notably a high-profile case against Israel .

In what could become a crucial factor for the Gaza case, where Israel claims its mass killings are part of a counter-terrorism operation, judges dismissed Myanmar’s claims of carrying out legitimate military operations against insurgents.

Genocide, defined after the Nazi Holocaust by a 1948 UN convention , is harder to prove than war crimes because it requires evidence of specific “intent” to destroy a national, ethnic, racial or religious group. Iwasawa said during the reading of the decision that the court was “fully convinced that Myanmar committed acts falling under … the genocide convention with an intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population in Myanmar”.

After the ruling, Britain’s foreign minister, Ed Miliband, said the government was expelling Myanmar’s defence attaché and called “urgently” for a session at the UN security council, the body that has the power to enforce ICJ rulings.

The case was raised by the Gambia, a Muslim-majority state, on behalf of Myanmar survivors. It rested on claims of genocidal statements and “patterns of conduct” that showed attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state, including gunning down people as they fled and blocking their return.

In January, the ICJ held closed-door sessions to hear from survivors who had travelled from camps in Bangladesh. More than a million Rohingya still live there, in the world’s largest refugee settlement, and fewer than 600,000 are estimated to remain in Buddhist-majority Myanmar.

Refugees who had fled to Bangladesh told the Guardian in 2017 of a massacre in the village of Tula Toli , where survivors described systematic shooting of civilians, mass graves and the drowning of children in a river. That village, which satellite footage later showed had been burned down , was one of several analysed by rights investigators and built a case for genocide.

During hearings, the Gambian justice minister, Dawda Jallow, told the court the case was not “about esoteric issues of international law”. “It is about real people, real stories and a real group of human beings,” said Jallow. “The Rohingya of Myanmar. They have been targeted for destruction.”

Legal experts see Thursday’s judgment as a key test for sexual violence in genocide assessments, as the convention says the crime can include acts with the intent to “prevent births”. Investigators have said gang-rapes and soldiers’ mutilation of women’s genitals were carried out intentionally and systematically to stop reproduction.

The court appeared to back that assessment, accusing the military of using sexual violence to “physically and mentally impair the willingness and ability of the [Rohingya] population to procreate”, referring to cultural stigma for rape survivors. Myanmar had also imposed other measures to restrict births, the court ruled, such as limits of two children per Rohingya family.

Myanmar has denied carrying out a genocide, claiming its actions targeted a Rohingya militant group that conducted guerrilla-style attacks. Its military responded with massive “clearance operations”.

However, judges rejected Myanmar’s claim that its actions were primarily intended as counter-terrorism operations, or even that they were an attempt to punish or forcibly displace the population but without committing genocide.

The country’s leader, Min Aung Hlaing, who headed the military during the 2016-17 attacks, has a pending arrest warrant from the international criminal court (ICC), which, unlike the ICJ, prosecutes individuals and not states, on allegations of crimes against humanity.

The former general overthrew the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in a 2021 coup, triggering a civil war that has left tens of thousands dead. He was installed as civilian president in April after elections that were widely discredited .

While the ICJ does not have the power to enforce rulings, its decisions are considered binding, carry diplomatic weight and can shape international action, including sanctions.…

title: Viagogo may have broken law on hidden fees, watchdog provisionally finds
text:
Ticket-reselling site Viagogo may have broken the law on hidden fees, the UK's competition body has said in a provisional finding.

The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) said it found that Viagogo failed to show consumers the total price upfront when they were buying tickets "and added fees later in the process, a practice known as drip pricing".

The CMA added that this was an initial finding, and it should not be assumed that the company had actually broken the law.

In a statement, Viagogo said it was co-operating fully with the CMA, adding that the investigation was continuing and "no final findings have been made".

The CMA said last year that it was investigating a number of companies over their online pricing practices, including Viagogo.

The competition watchdog said it had looked into the experience of UK fans buying tickets for events such as concerts and sport on three websites that operate under the Viagogo brand.

"The CMA believes that mandatory costs such as taxes and booking fees were added at later stages of the checkout process and not included in the total price from the start," it said.

"Drip pricing can cause fans to be caught out by extra charges and buy tickets they might not otherwise have selected, had they been able to compare prices accurately from the start."

The CMA said Viagogo would now have an opportunity to consider its findings and respond before a final decision is made.

"This is an ongoing investigation and no final findings have been made," Viagogo said in a statement.

"We have engaged constructively with the CMA and continue to cooperate fully with its investigation."

The CMA has powers to tackle anti-competitive behaviour. It can now decide if consumer laws have been broken - rather than having to go through the courts.

Drip pricing is one of the practices the CMA has been focusing on particularly.

On Wednesday, it said it was investigating three companies , external over the issue, and in August it announced that the Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School had been engaged in the practice.

In general, the CMA can impose penalties of up to 10% of global turnover for a breach of consumer law. However, it will consider a number of factors, including the severity of conduct, before deciding on the size of the penalty.

In June this year, the watchdog ordered rival ticket reseller StubHub UK to refund more than 50,000 customers and pay a £900,000 fine for not showing people the total price upfront when buying tickets.

StubHub UK received a 40% reduction to its financial penalty after it admitted to breaking the law and agreed to settle the case early with the CMA.

title: 'Passion has no age. Class is timeless' – Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali confirm Domenico Pozzovivo will continue racing at the age of 44
author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
text:
Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali have confirmed that Domenico Pozzovivo will race on with the team next year, the Italian climber continuing in the peloton past his 44th birthday.

"Some riders are part of a team. Others are part of cycling history. Domenico Pozzovivo will continue racing in Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali colours in 2027! Passion has no age. Class is timeless," the team announced on Wednesday.

Pozzovivo, who turns 44 on November 30, has been racing since 2005, with next year marking his 22nd season as a pro. He retired at the end of 2024 as he and his wife Valentina welcomed their first child, Diana, before returning in April on a one-year deal.

Pozzovivo didn't race the Giro d'Italia in 2026 after his team didn't receive an invite, but he told that he's hoping to make a record-breaking 19th appearance at his home Grand Tour next May.

"Now I'm at 18, tied with Wladimiro Panizza, and... yes, I'd like to," he said. "Also because nowadays it's rare for a professional career to last beyond 12-14 years. So it would be a record that, while not unbeatable, could last a long time.

"Competition is the foundation of sport, and yes, I confess that it makes me happy. Finishing ahead of someone less than half my age doubles the satisfaction."

Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali look good for a Giro wildcard invitation next season alongside Polti-VisitiMalta, with Italy's other ProTeam, Bardiani CSF-7 Saber, not eligible for an invitation after missing the top 30 in the UCI rankings.

Pozzovivo would be a leader for the team if they are invited. He finished the season with the second-most UCI points of any rider on the roster, only behind Serbian sprinter Dušan Rajović, and this year achieved a series of eye-catching results at the age of 43.

Highlights of his 2026 season included third-place finishes at the Giro dell'Appennino, GP Beiras a Serra da Estrela, the Czech Tour, and a fourth place at the Mercan'Tour Classic Alpes-Maritimes.

"Between training and races, a million kilometres – actually, even more. At least 1.1 million. And I still haven’t stopped," he told .

"Training isn't a big deal for me, and I enjoy cycling. My performance, considering my age, is decent. So I turn the tables: why shouldn't I? Besides, I'm naturally drawn to challenging myself and my limits. That's the main thing."

Pozzovivo said that he had to negotiate with his wife to continue racing. He's balanced family life with time on the bike, while he has also completed his third degree (studies in nutrition sciences have followed previous degrees in business economics and sports science), with a fourth possibly upcoming.

"It was a fairly long 'negotiation', so to speak. When I stopped, at the end of 2024, one of the reasons was to be as close as possible to my daughter, who was about to be born," he said.

"But I started again because I realised that things could be reconciled, given that cycling is still important but no longer comes first. I'm trying to put it all together, and I think I can do it.

"If you love studying, and I do, it's right to continue doing so because staying up-to-date is essential – keeping up with the latest discoveries in practice. Specifically, I've delved deeper into nutrition sciences because it's something that, in endurance sports, now affects performance by 50%.

"Next year I'd like to take the state exam to become a nutritional biologist. To answer your question... Maybe, but I don't rule out the possibility that I might be interested in a Master's degree."

Now, however, Pozzovivo will turn his focus to training for 2027 and that possible return to the Giro d'Italia, where he's finished in the top 10 on seven occasions. Will it be his final season on the bike?

"We'll see. It's not a given," he concluded.

title: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza
author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
text:
First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu

The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.

Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road , Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.

An Israeli military spokesperson said troops were carrying out an operation targeting “Hamas infrastructure” west of the yellow line in central Gaza .

The military ​has not commented extensively on the operation, which came as the Israeli opposition politician, Gadi Eisenkot, has been seeking to form a government without the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his political reputation on promises to keep Israel safe.

A Gaza security source told AFP there was “intense Israeli artillery shelling” north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza “amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday”.

Hamas condemned the Israeli raid and the forced displacement of Palestinians as “a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement” and a dangerous escalation. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to Hamas’s statement.

Residents reported hearing tank fire in the area. Palestinian medics said one person was killed in an Israeli airstrike near the site of the raid.

In separate incidents on Wednesday, Palestinian medics said two people were killed by Israeli fire, one in Deir al-Balah and the other in Gaza City. The Israeli military said it was unaware of any incident in Deir al-Balah and had struck a militant in Gaza City.

Israel has stepped up its attacks on Hamas, which it says has been regrouping and rearming. Hamas has accused Israel of trying to derail the US-brokered ceasefire agreed in October 2025.

Israeli strikes have continued since the ceasefire, and Hamas remains armed.

Last week, an Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.

The body overseeing Donald Trump’s plan to end the war in Gaza has accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities, leaving Palestinians in dire conditions and the ceasefire at risk of collapse.

In its second report to the UN security council since the truce began 13 months ago, the Trump-led Board of Peace said the gap between what was agreed and what was happening on the ground remained the biggest threat to the deal. The report, seen by Reuters, warned that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely”.

Gaza’s health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire came into effect. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.

Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel launched its military campaign in response to the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed.

Reuters and AFP contributed to this report

title: Mauricio Pochettino calls for Manchester United to show no fear against Liverpool
author: Will Unwin
text:
New head coach’s first game is at Anfield on Sunday

‘We are going there with the idea to win and be brave’

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to have “no fear” when they travel to Anfield on Sunday for his first game. The Argentinian does not want his players to take a backward step as he targets a fast start.

United are 18th in the Premier League and Liverpool fourth but the head coach will not accept any self-doubt. Pochettino is known for being attack-minded and is keen to instil those ideals, but will have had only three days with the players since replacing Michael Carrick.

“We are going to Anfield with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United ,” Pochettino told the club’s website. “The history talks for us, and what we need to expect. We need to be sure that we are brave and we are protagonists and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.”

Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday after an overnight flight, having taken charge of his final USA match against Haiti . He toured the training ground and held meetings with senior staff and players not on international duty.

Members of Pochettino’s staff were in place earlier in the week as they seek to revitalise a team with one league win. Pochettino is waiting for United to ratify the appointment of Sílvia Tuyà, a strength and conditioning coach who worked with him with the USA. She travelled with him by private jet to Manchester but was not named among the staff later in the day.

“We need to go little by little, step by step,” Pochettino said. “We cannot go too fast but also we need to, at the same time, attack the priorities to build something.”

He said it was important he and his staff adapt to the culture of the club. “And then, with this sense of knowing the history of the club, try to create all together, because we are all different, a culture, a philosophy that can respect that identity, the history of the club. But at the same time, performing. If we don’t perform, the responsibility is mine.”

Pochettino has coveted the United job and is a keen admirer of Sir Alex Ferguson, whom he describes as “the best coach in history”. Since the Scot’s retirement in 2013, United have failed to match his success but Pochettino said he was looking at “the potential of the club”. The weight of past achievements has hindered individuals over the past 13 years.

“The players need to express their talent,” Pochettino said. “We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now: it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it’s too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your teammates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.”

He sounded an upbeat note, saying: “With the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

United’s total borrowings have risen to £784.5m, with long-term debt up by almost £100m over the past year. Figures published for the three months to 30 September show long-term borrowings of £577.4m, compared with £481.2m 12 months earlier. United’s cash reserves fell from £80.5m to £55.5m during the same period despite an increase in revenue.

The club reported a quarterly net loss of £18.1m, compared with £6.6m ​in ​the same period a year earlier. Revenue rose by 4% to £146m.

title: Eight injured after driver in Israel repeatedly rams car into Palestinians
author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
text:
Arab MPs accuse politicians of fuelling hostility as footage shows driver accelerating towards Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim

Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel .

Footage shared on social media appears to show the car accelerating towards people, all Palestinians, at several locations in the city, striking them before driving away. Three of those injured were in moderate condition, and several of the victims were women leaving a nearby wedding, the Times of Israel reported .

Haaretz has reported that investigators are examining whether the driver struck people deliberately. Avi Levy, a police district commander, said the incident appeared to be a hit-and-run and that the driver had tested positive for drugs. He said the Shin Bet security service was taking part in the investigation and said: “As of this moment, nothing is coming up. The suspect has no criminal record.”

The incident prompted Arab lawmakers and activists to accuse Israeli politicians of fuelling hostility towards Arab citizens. Benjamin Netanyahu has called Arab parties “terror supporters” and said partnering with them would put Israel’s security at risk. The parties won a record 19 seats in the Knesset in the country’s recent election.

Yousef Jabareen, the chair of the Joint List, said the incident “raises difficult questions about the claim that the driver lost control”. He said: “I’ve been warning for weeks that the incitement against Arab citizens will turn into assaults and even assassinations.”

Said Issa, a community activist in Kafr Qasim, described the incident as an “act of terror”. “Someone who loses control of his vehicle might hit one or two vehicles, but not multiple people in several different places,” Issa said. “The attacker struck at four locations, one after the other.”

In a separate incident in the occupied West Bank, the Palestinian foreign ministry called on Monday for an Israeli settler to be held accountable after eight Palestinians were run over and injured in Tuqu , south-east of Bethlehem. Local sources told the Anadolu news agency that the driver had first struck three young men, then returned and ran over five others who had gathered to help them.

title: Tour de Romandie saved as Primeo Energie steps in as sponsor for both women’s and men’s races
author: Owen Rogers
text:
After a lack of funds was cited as a major contributing factor in the cancellation of the 2026 Tour de Romandie Féminin , the race will return in 2027 with Primeo Energie stepping up to sponsor both women’s and men’s races.

The Swiss electricity company have sponsored the races’ mountains classification jerseys since 2022, the first year of the women’s race, but will now be the main sponsor of both events for the next two editions.

Even before the 2026 race, the organisation was in trouble, hoping to address a 10% budget shortfall by attracting Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates). But a week after he won four of the five stages and the general classification, organisers, Chassot Concept SA, announced the postponement of the 2026 women’s race.

"This postponement also aims to preserve the Foundation's financial stability and, ultimately, to guarantee the quality and long-term viability of the event," organisers said at the time .

Now, with Primeo Energie on board, not only is the men’s race secure, but the women’s event will return in 2027, with the three-day stage race due to start on September 10th.

"We have seen just how deeply the Tour de Romandie is rooted in the hearts of the people of French-speaking Switzerland," Primeo Energie’s CEO, Cédric Christmann, said. "We are strengthening our presence in a region where we intend to continue our growth.

"Supporting the women’s race is also particularly important to me; women’s cycling deserves more attention - much like the energy sector, especially regarding technical roles and leadership positions."

Unlike the men’s race, which began in 1947, the women’s race has a short history, starting as recently as 2022. Then Ashleigh Moolman-Pasio beat Annemiek van Vleuten on the mountain stage to the ski centre at Thyon 2000, going on to take the only WorldTour general classification success of her career.

Held in 2025, the most recent edition was won by home rider Elise Chabby (FDJ-SUEZ). The race also witnessed the emergence of Paula Blasi, who won the opening day mountain time trial, collecting her first WorldTour victory. However, the race was undermined when five teams were excluded from the race before the start .

While details of the women’s race are yet to be released, organisers chose the sponsorship announcement to publish details of the 80th edition of the men’s race, which will start with its traditional prologue on Tuesday, April 27 and feature a number of circuit-based stages.

"We have opted for loop-style stages, with each one taking place almost entirely within a single canton," said organiser Richard Chassot.

"This allows the public to see the riders multiple times in a festive atmosphere. This format also addresses safety requirements, which are becoming increasingly complex and costly."

Stage 1 - Romont - Romont (170.1km)

Stage 3 - Vully-les-Lacs - Vully-les-Lacs, ITT (14.6km)

title: Tour Colombia returns for 2027 after two-year break with multiple WorldTour teams expected to race
author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
text:
The early-season Tour Colombia returns to the calendar in 2027, with the race's fifth edition set to run January 26-31.

The race was founded in 2018 as the Colombia Oro y Paz and has run editions in 2019, 2020, and 2024. It was cancelled in both 2025 and 2026 due to financial difficulties.

It's back next season, however, with its return announced in September. Last week, the race was unveiled in a presentation in Medellín attended by former winners Egan Bernal and Sergio Higuita, as well as a host of other Colombian cycling stars, including Santiago Buitrago , Fernando Gaviria, Nairo Quintana, and Rigoberto Urán.

Colombian outlet has revealed that WorldTour teams Netcompany Ineos and EF Education-EasyPost will be taking part. It's likely, then, that Bernal, Harold Tejada, Iván Sosa, and Juan Felipe Rodríguez will be racing.

title: Nvidia approaches Arm boss Rene Haas in search for new CEO
author: Lauren Almeida
text:
CEO of Cambridge-based firm viewed as leading contender to replace co-founder Jensen Huang according to reports

Nvidia’s headhunters have reportedly approached the chief executive of the Cambridge-based chip company Arm, in its search for a new leader after Jensen Huang’s dramatic exit.

Heidrick & Struggles, the recruiting firm hired by the company’s board, has started contacting potential candidates, according to Bloomberg.

It reported that Rene Haas, who joined Arm in 2013 and became chief executive in 2022, is among those approached.

Nvidia is searching for a replacement for Huang, one of the firm’s founders, who resigned last week after he admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman accused of spying for China .

Haas, 64, is viewed as the leading contender for the top job at Nvidia , having previously worked at the $3.6tn (£2.8tn) company for seven years as the general manager of its computing products.

Reports suggest that other potential candidates include: Ian Buck, an Nvidia vice-president; Lisa Su, AMD’s chief executive; and Johny Srouji, Apple’s chief hardware officer.

Arm, which is listed in New York but retains its global headquarters in Cambridge, has about 500 users of its chip designs worldwide, including Nvidia, Apple, Samsung and Qualcomm. The company employs more than 7,000 staff, including more than 3,000 in the UK. It is the biggest tech firm headquartered in Britain, now valued at $196bn.

Haas told a tech conference in Austin on Wednesday that Huang was “a legend”. “What he built at Nvidia is historic,” he said. “You don’t have many champions like that.”

Nvidia has sought to curb speculation that Huang could return to his role, after he said on Tuesday that he would be willing to come back.

He wrote in a statement: “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

It came after US president, Donald Trump, and Silicon Valley insiders – including Elon Musk, prominent venture capitalists and the disgraced Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick – called for Huang’s reinstatement.

However, the Nvidia chair, Harvey Jones, confirmed at the company’s quarterly earnings results this week that the board “ does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO ”.

Jones said that “while this was an unexpected transition … the board is proactively dealing with the consequences”.

Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer, was named interim CEO last week and presented the financial results on Tuesday, which showed that its quarterly revenue had doubled from the same period a year ago to $115.84bn.

Huang agreed on Tuesday to appear before the House of Representatives foreign affairs committee, the select committee on the Chinese Communist party and the intelligence committee for transcribed interviews in early December. Nvidia also faces an investigation by the US Securities and Exchange Commission over its business in China, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.

Nvidia and Arm were approached for comment.

title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
author: Rebecca Ratcliffe
text:
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits

Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa , on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer.

The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago , when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park , owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. Ivanishvili has filled the park with ancient, giant trees from Georgia, transporting them by boat along the Black Sea.

The export of the Kenyan baobabs was initially blocked after an outcry by environmentalists, who condemned their export as biopiracy , but later allowed to go ahead.

Otherwise, such exports are very rare, say experts. David Newton, programme office director for east and southern Africa for Traffic, an NGO that monitors the trade in wild animals and plants, said: “It is very unusual to see baobabs being used as ornamental plants … mainly because they are exceptionally difficult to dig out of the ground and transport, and then to successfully re-establish.”

Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, who has led efforts to replant the South African trees, said she believes they have a good chance of surviving if they are replanted quickly. The winter months of May to October, when the trees lose their leaves and are dormant, is a good time to move them.

“As soon as spring starts [in November], the trees use their water to flush their new leaves, and that’s when we need to get them into the ground as soon as possible,” she said.

The rescue mission has faced delays because of the challenges associated with moving such large trees, which are transported on special trucks capable of carrying abnormal loads. The five baobabs weigh between 19 and 29 tonnes, have a diameter of up to 4.5 metres (15ft) and a height of up to 12.5 metres.

Baobabs, known as the tree of life, are protected under South African law, which means a permit is required to cut or disturb them.

“A baobab isn’t just part of an ecosystem, it is an ecosystem in itself,” said Wambui Ippolito, a landscape designer, lecturer and horticulturist from Kenya. “These trees are biodiversity anchors.”

Animals ranging from bats and bush babies, to grey-headed parrots and the southern ground hornbill shelter in its cavities, while elephants, monkeys and warthogs feast on its fruit.

The trees have huge cultural importance, added Ippolito. “It has always been a sacred tree in Africa. It doesn’t matter where you go: Senegal, Mali, Ghana – wherever you go, if there is a community around a baobab tree, that tree is sacred,” she said. “Somebody’s great-great-great-great-great-grandparents sat under that tree, and it is part of human history in that area.”

Baobabs have shallow roots, which means they do not need to be planted very deeply, and these regrow fairly quickly, said Venter. Once replanted, the trees will be stabilised with cables and protected by electric fences to prevent damage from elephants.

The trees are thought to be between 200 and 300 years old. “Baobabs easily reach 1,000 years old, so they’ve got a few hundred years ahead of them if they survive,” said Venter.

A criminal case has been opened against the owner of a landscaping company allegedly responsible for the illegal harvesting and transportation of the trees.

TotalEnergies is leaving Netcompany-Ineos in a pivot to women's racing. (Photo: ASPER JACOBS / BELGA MAG / Belga / AFP via Getty Images)

Netcompany-Ineos will lose TotalEnergies as a backer in 2027 just as the former Tour de France powerhouse tries to rebuild its challenge for the yellow jersey.

The departure — first reported by The Athletic and subsequently confirmed by the team — ends a partnership that began ahead of the 2025 Tour. The French energy giant reportedly contributed more than €10 million annually.

That leaves a major hole to fill, but the team did not say reveal the exit will affect its budget.

“We’re grateful to everyone at TotalEnergies for their support and commitment since joining us ahead of the 2025 Tour de France. They’ve been valued partners, and we’re proud to have represented the TotalEnergies brand across two seasons of racing,” a Netcompany-Ineos spokesperson said in a statement to the media.

It’s a financial hit as the team is undergoing a rebuilding effort to regain its spot in the Tour de France conversation.

Danish technology company Netcompany joined as title sponsor in May, reportedly worth around €20 million per season. Ineos remains the team owner and has been searching for new financial partners to help ease the financial cost of the WorldTour team.

Team officials did not reveal how this will impact the team’s budget for 2027.

The team saw high turnover during this year’s transfer season, with Filippo Ganna, Ben Turner, Andrew August, Magnus Sheffield, and Artem Shimdt among several riders leaving.

Though there were no marquee signings, it picked up highly touted junior world champion Benjamín Noval and Riley Sheehan among nine new arrivals for 2027.

At its peak, during the Sky/Ineos era, it won seven Tours with eight different riders from 2012 to 2019, but has not reached the Paris podium since Geraint Thomas finished third in 2022.

Expected race leader Oscar Onley missed this year’s race due to a shoulder injury, and Egan Bernal’s 20th was the team’s top GC.

TotalEnergies, meanwhile, is pivoting its cycling resources into women’s racing .

It exited Jean-René Bernaudeau’s men’s ProTeam squad, which lated landed replacement sponsor XEFI for three seasons through 2029.

This week, the French company also committed to five seasons as co-title title sponsor of Demi Vollering’s team from 2027.

title: EDF snaps up 1.3m more customers after Utilita takeover
author: Jillian Ambrose
text:
Great Britain’s fourth-largest energy supplier brings account base up to 6m after purchase of pay-as-you-go supplier

EDF Energy will grow its share of the UK’s household energy market to more than 6m customer accounts after snapping up the pay-as-you-go supplier Utilita.

Great Britain’s fourth-largest energy supplier expects to complete the takeover early next year, adding 1.3m accounts to its customer base and taking on Utilita’s 1,500 staff. The price of the deal was undisclosed.

The pair will continue to serve their customers independently until the deal concludes. Utilita customers will be contacted about any changes to their service.

After the deal, EDF has promised to continue to operate from Utilita’s headquarters near Southampton which is the base for about 600of Utilita’s employees.

EDF, which is owned by the French state, set out the takeover plans a year after it completed a deal to take on 47,000 standard credit accounts from Utilita which said it hoped to sharpen its focus on smart pay-as-you-go customers.

The deal is likely to have helped bolster Utilita’s financial position, which briefly fell short of the industry regulator Ofgem’s tougher new financial resilience tests in an industry assessment in September 2025.

Utilita confirmed that it was one of five suppliers which had failed to meet Ofgem’s financial rules last year, but said it was able to comply with the standards within months of the regulator’s red flag.

For EDF, the deal will help to bolster its business as most large suppliers continue to lose customers to smaller rivals. EDF lost about 280,000 customer accounts in the year after July 2025, while British Gas, Scottish Power and E.ON Next were also losing customers. Octopus Energy , the country’s largest supplier, is the only big energy company which has continued to grow its market share.

Utilita was founded in 2003 as a specialist prepay energy supplier, and became the first supplier to install a smart meter in 2008.

Its pioneering approach to smart metering helped the company to modernise pay-as-you-go energy by allowing customers to top-up via an app, website, or by phone rather than visit a corner shop or post office to pay for credit on a plastic card or key.

Simone Rossi, the chief executive of EDF’s UK business, said Utilita would bring “further expertise” to the supplier, marking “a significant step” in EDF’s ambition to grow its UK customer business.

“Together, we will have the scale and skills to keep developing services and support for the households who rely on us,” Rossi said.

Bill Bullen, the founder of Utilita, said the deal would ensure that Utilita could continue to provide “best-in-class smart prepay solutions to Britain’s households”.

Last month, German energy group E.ON Next completed a deal to buy struggling UK rival Ovo after the deal was approved by Britain’s competition watchdog.

The deal comes as households prepare for a sharp rise in energy bills this winter. On Wednesday, the consultancy Cornwall Insight forecast the quarterly industry price cap would jump 26% from January to the equivalent of £2,166 a year for a typical household.

title: BAE to slash 1,000 jobs across head office and air business
author: Lauren Almeida and Jasper Jolly
text:
Job cuts to exclude shop floor, aircraft maintenance and trainees but move prompts calls for more orders to support British defence giant

BAE Systems has announced plans to cut more than 1,000 jobs from its workforce, triggering calls for ministers to place extra orders with Britain’s biggest defence contractor.

The company said it is aiming to cut 1,070 jobs at its head office and air business in the UK, as it tries to meet customer demands for “greater speed and efficiency in getting critical capabilities into the hands of those who need them”.

The cuts represent about 2% of its 50,000 strong workforce in the UK, which includes about 18,500 in its air business and about 1,000 in its head office in London. They will be made through voluntary redundancies and will exclude people working on the shop floor, aircraft maintenance at RAF bases and early career trainees.

A spokesperson for BAE said the cuts represented the “next stage of our ongoing focus on enhancing our agility and competitiveness, so we can help to maximise the value of every pound our customers spend on defence.

“We recognise that this news may be unsettling for our people and we’re focused on achieving potential workforce reductions through a voluntary process,” they said.

BAE last year received an order for 20 Typhoon fighter jets from Turkey, in a deal announced at the factory by Keir Starmer. However, that order is thought to provide only two years of work at the Lancashire factories – not enough to sustain jobs until production starts on the next generation of fighters. BAE will lead production of the sixth-generation Tempest fighter in an alliance with Italy and Japan.

A source with knowledge of the matter said that the job cuts were linked to uncertainty over the Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jet programme , more than cost-cutting.

The move comes even as BAE has benefited from a boom in defence spending since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Last month, the company told its investors it had secured £33bn in orders so far this year and that it expected further contracts before the end of 2026. It also raised its free cashflow guidance for its financial year by 10%, from about £2bn to £3bn.

Sharon Graham, the general secretary of the union Unite, warned that there would not be a manufacturing industry left in the UK “if the government doesn’t start making critical decisions”.

“To stop the erosion of defence jobs and get the growth we need, the government needs to announce contracts for British-built Typhoons and Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) immediately,” she said.

BAE unveiled the uncrewed CCA – which is named Brontanax – at the Farnborough International airshow in July.

Andrew Snowden, a Conservative MP in Lancashire where BAE has two air manufacturing hubs, echoed Graham’s call for more government support.

He told the Lancashire Post: “The government should act now to support BAE by placing orders for British-built Typhoons and Collaborative Combat Aircraft, giving skilled workers and the supply chain here in Lancashire a clear pipeline of work.”

It comes with the government also under pressure to reach a decision on its Skynet military satellite replacement. American weapons maker Lockheed Martin was thought to be the Ministry of Defence’s preferred choice, but ministers have delayed the choice after Unite argued it would lead to UK job cuts at rival Airbus’s existing factories.

An MoD spokesperson said: “We know that any potential voluntary redundancies can cause concerns and our thoughts are with those potentially affected.

“This government is delivering the biggest boost in defence spending since the cold ar, having already agreed £4bn worth of investments since July.

“This includes awarding BAE a £708m contract extension to lead the Global Combat Air Programme developments and supporting the £8bn contract to supply Turkey with 20 Typhoon jets last year, which sustains 6,000 jobs at two BAE sites.”

title: Giro d’Italia Taps MAAP to Make the Pink Jersey in 2027
author: ahood
text:
MAAP is linking up with the Giro d'Italia in bold new deal. (Photo: Gruber Images/MAAP)

MAAP will make and design the Giro d’Italia’s pink jersey in 2027 in a big move for the Melbourne company that built its name on minimalist graphics and high-end performance.

The multi-year agreement with RCS Sport includes the classification jerseys at the Giro d’Italia , Giro d’Italia Women and Giro Next Gen, including the iconic maglia rosa .

“MAAP was founded in Melbourne just 12 years ago. In 2027, we’ll design the ‘maglia rosa,'” cofounder Jarrad Smith said in the announcement. “It’s the race that got me into road cycling.”

MAAP will also supply technical apparel for all RCS races, in both men’s and women’s editions at Strade Bianche, Milano-Sanremo, Il Lombardia, Tirreno-Adriatico, Giro-E, Milano-Torino, Il Giro d’Abruzzo, and GranPiemonte.

Financial terms were not disclosed Thursday when officials confirmed the deal.

MAAP built a following among younger cyclists with its trademark graphics and street-wear cred coupled with top-end performance quality.

The company quickly grew organically and was built by word of mouth into what’s now a global brand.

For RCS, the pivot comes as the Italian grand tour is trying to get younger fans to start adding the Giro into their social media feeds.

“We are confident that the new jerseys, which will be unveiled soon, will generate great interest among all cycling fans, and particularly among younger generations,” said Paolo Bellino, CEO and general manager of RCS Sports and Events.

No one knows. Thursday’s announcement only confirmed the deal.

“The partnership seeks to bridge the deep traditions of European racing with contemporary culture through performance and design,” a statement read.

Based on the PR, it also sounds like there will be special-edition apparel and accessories for each race via “race capsules.”

The first jerseys will be revealed ahead of Milano-Sanremo in March.

The Giro’s switch is part of a leader’s jersey reshuffle across all three grand tours.

Castelli , which supplied the Giro’s pink jersey through this year, will replace Santini at both the Tour de France and the Vuelta a España in 2027.

The Tour is reviving the Castelli partnership that dates back to the days of Greg LeMond and Miguel Indurain in a deal that ran from 1989 to 1994.

The Giro and MAAP link up after the brand worked with the GreenEdge organization and Jayco-AlUla starting in 2025.

Its Pro Aero race suit has been part of stage wins at all three men’s grand tours, the Tour de France Femmes, and a string of WorldTour classics.

Now it will hit the podium every day across the RCS Sport race portfolio.

title: 'A bold new visual era' for the maglia rosa as MAAP strikes deal to produce Giro d'Italia leaders' jerseys
author: Owen Rogers
text:
Australian cycling kit company MAAP is promising an eye-catching revamp of the Giro d’Italia leaders’ jerseys after agreeing a multi-year partnership with organisers RCS to provide apparel across their range of races.

As well as the men’s and women's Giro d'Italia, the agreement will also see the brand providing jerseys for RCS’s other Italian stage races, including Tirreno Adriatico and the Giro Next Gen.

There will also be jerseys for one-day events like Milan-San Remo, Strade Bianche, and Il Lombardia, though they won’t be worn in the race or awarded to winners.

MAAP, which was only founded in 2014, first entered the European pro peloton in 2024, producing a striking design for women’s Continental team Lifeplus-Wahoo, before going further with the current purple Jayco-AlUla and Liv-AlUla Jayco team kits.

To continue in that eye-catching vein, MAAP is promising "a bold new visual era for the most beautiful Grand Tours".

understands the new pink jersey design for men’s and women’s Giro d'Italia will be a significant departure from the old produced by Castelli, though it will not be revealed until sometime in the New Year.

"The partnership seeks to bridge the deep traditions of European racing with contemporary culture through performance and design," MAAP’s press release states.

"Bringing a progressive perspective to some of cycling's most iconic symbols, MAAP will honour the heritage of these events while challenging conventions through a new approach to technical apparel and visual expression."

It’s been a remarkable rise for MAAP, which was founded in 2014 in the Australian city of Melbourne and has always produced kit that looks a little different to that of other companies. Their first team partnership was for Australian Continental team State of the Matter, before partnering with Trinity Racing in 2019.

"From the start, we set out to make the world’s best cycling apparel, paired with a design language that lights up the sport," said company founder Jarrad Smith.

"The Giro d’Italia has shaped the performance and aesthetic of cycling for more than a century, and it holds a special place in my heart. It’s the race that got me into road cycling. Stepping into that living history, and helping progress the Maglia Rosa and some of cycling’s most storied races, is a defining milestone and a privilege. It’s also a statement of our respect for the sport’s history and our passion for where it can go."

CEO and General Manager of RCS Sports and Events Paolo Bellino said: "MAAP is a young and ambitious company, it stands out for its use of technologically advanced materials and its strong design identity. We are confident that the new jerseys, which will be unveiled soon, will generate great interest among all cycling fans, and particularly among younger generations.

"We hope that this partnership with MAAP will lead us into a new era, one that is even more modern and innovative, while continuing to respect the great tradition of the Giro d’Italia and our races."

The deal comes hot on the heels of Castelli’s partnership and sponsorship agreement with ASO to provide leaders’ jerseys for the Tour de France , Tour de France Femmes and their other races, including both men’s and women’s Vuelta a España, though it is thought the sponsorship element of MAAP’s deal is absent.
